title: Hummingbird load probe — microburst + background interleave
content:
Purpose:
Quick private scratch to capture a weird tail we saw on the internal canary last week. Goal is to reproduce small (3–10 req) microbursts arriving on top of a steady background stream and measure p50/p95/p99 with/without adaptive-priming + KV cache.

Hypothesis:
1) Tiny bursts interleaved with steady low-QPS create priming collisions in renderer thread + KV cache churn that blow up p99.
2) Lightweight priority lanes that preempt batch assembly for very small requests will recover p99 without hurting overall throughput.

Setup:
- Model: redwood/gpt-medium-compat (seq_len 512, q8_0 quantized build)
- Node: single dedicated GPU (A10G-sim), 32GB
- Harness: custom replay harness (nodejs) that can inject background QPS + burst overlay; measured via local prometheus scrape and direct histogram export
- Requests: small chat turns (avg 40 tokens output), tokenization overhead ~12 tokens
- Three configs:
  A. baseline: continuous batching, no KV cache
  B. cache: prefix/KV caching enabled (TTL 30s), continuous batching
  C. adaptive: cache + adaptive-priority lanes (priority threshold 8 tokens, max preemption 2 batches/min)
- Workload pattern: background 6 QPS steady + bursts: every 20s inject 1–8 concurrent requests over 400ms window (Poisson-gated). Run for 30m.

Commands (harness):
- node run_probe.js --model redwood/gpt-medium-compat --background 6 --burst-profile hummingbird --duration 1800 --out raw_hb_A.json
- change flags: --kv-cache --adaptive-priority etc.

Raw observations (30m windows):
Config A (baseline): throughput steady ~6–8 QPS. p50=110ms, p95=420ms, p99=1.32s. Visible spike tails after bursts where 0.5–1% requests hit >2s (collects as cold-path warms). CPU thread wakeups correlated with incoming burst start (trace ids flagged).

Config B (kv cache): p50=95ms, p95=360ms, p99=980ms. KV hit rate during bursts ~64% (falling from 88% between bursts). Still observed a long tail cluster ~1.8s on ~0.2% of requests concentrated right after burst windows.

Config C (kv + adaptive): p50=92ms, p95=240ms, p99=410ms. Throughput same baseline. Tail cluster reduced dramatically. Observed fewer wakeup amplifications; batching latency decreased for small requests due to preemption avoiding batch stuffing.

Interpretation / notes:
- The long tails are not pure cold-starts — they happen even with KV hits present. Likely cause: batch assembly + renderer lock contention when multiple tiny requests race to claim batch slots and trigger hot-path context swaps.
- KV cache helps but only for requests that reuse the same prefix; microbursts with diverse prompts still produce contention.
- Adaptive-priority lane that allows up-to-N small requests to jump ahead of large batched assembly solves the majority of the tail without measurable impact on throughput.

Telemetry highlights:
- Trace snapshots attached in GH PR (see linked_artifacts) show thread stacks: many threads in sys_sched_wait followed by long epoll wake latency ~40–80ms during cluster spikes.
- Heap/GC not the culprit: GC pauses <5ms and not correlated with tail windows.

Quick actionable next steps:
- Add a targeted experiment: increase background QPS to 12 and run same three configs to confirm adaptive approach scales. (Run id: hb_20251108_up12)
- Tweak adaptive preemption budget: test budgets {1,2,4} preemptions per minute to see sweet spot.
- Add request fingerprinting to estimate effective prefix reuse; measure whether microburst diversity threshold predicts KV efficacy.
- Draft a short runbook for SRE: how to enable adaptive lanes at deploy-time and safe rollback knobs.

Questions / open items:
- Should we default adaptive lanes on for dedicated pools? My gut: yes for small-request-heavy customers, but need canary for model-variant interactions.
- Need to check cross-model memory amplification when preemption moves context more often.

Notes-to-self:
- Save raw_hb_A.json/B/C and processed histograms in /tmp/hummingbird-run-20251106/ before deleting.
- Create dashboard: p99 by 10s window aligned to burst events, overlay KV hit rate and preemption events.

Conclusion (working):
Adaptive-priority + KV cache together seem to reduce p99 by ~60–70% in this microburst + background interleave pattern. Reasonable candidate for a default SLO-focused mitigation for small-request workloads. Still want to validate with higher background QPS and with multi-GPU setups.

Signed: Nadia
